```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center", dpi = 150)
source("data_prep.R")          # shared loader, split, and scaling
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

CORR_THRESHOLD <- 0.90         # |r| at or above this = "highly correlated"
FIG_DIR <- file.path("outputs", "figures")
TAB_DIR <- file.path("outputs", "tables")
dir.create(FIG_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(TAB_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Colorblind-checked pair: benign = blue, malignant = orange
DX_COLORS <- c(Benign = "#2a78d6", Malignant = "#eb6834")

theme_eda <- theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#e4e3df", linewidth = 0.3),
        strip.text         = element_text(size = 9, color = "#0b0b0b"),
        axis.text          = element_text(color = "#52514e"),
        plot.title         = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5),
        plot.background    = element_rect(fill = "#fcfcfb", color = NA),
        legend.position    = "top")
```

# Data

We use the Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Diagnostic) dataset (Wolberg, Mangasarian, Street, & Street, 1993)
from the [UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/17). Each observation is a
digitized image of a fine needle aspirate (FNA) of a breast mass. Ten properties of the cell nuclei are each
summarized by their mean, standard error (`se`), and "worst" value (mean of the three largest), giving
30 continuous features.

```{r load}
df <- load_data()
df$dx <- factor(ifelse(df$diagnosis == 1, "Malignant", "Benign"),
                levels = c("Benign", "Malignant"))

# Long format: one row per (sample, feature), used for plotting
long <- data.frame(
  feature = factor(rep(FEATURES, each = nrow(df)), levels = FEATURES),
  value   = unlist(df[FEATURES], use.names = FALSE),
  dx      = rep(df$dx, times = length(FEATURES))
)
```

The data contain `r nrow(df)` observations: `r sum(df$diagnosis == 1)` malignant
(`r round(100 * mean(df$diagnosis), 1)`%) and `r sum(df$diagnosis == 0)` benign, with
`r sum(is.na(df))` missing values.

# Preprocessing

All preprocessing lives in `data_prep.R`, which every team member sources so that we all work with
identical data:

1. **Recoding.** `diagnosis` is recoded so that malignant = 1 and benign = 0.
2. **Stratified split.** 20% of each class is sampled separately for the test set using a fixed seed (`r RANDOM_SEED`),
   so both sets keep the same malignant-to-benign ratio.
3. **Standardization.** Features are centered and scaled using the **training set's** means and standard
   deviations only. The test set is transformed with those same values, so no information from the test set
   enters model training.

```{r split}
sp <- get_splits()

split_summary <- data.frame(
  Set         = c("Train", "Test"),
  n           = c(length(sp$y_train), length(sp$y_test)),
  Malignant   = c(sum(sp$y_train), sum(sp$y_test)),
  Benign      = c(sum(sp$y_train == 0), sum(sp$y_test == 0)),
  `% malignant` = round(100 * c(mean(sp$y_train), mean(sp$y_test)), 1),
  check.names = FALSE
)
kable(split_summary, caption = "Stratified train/test split")
```

```{r scale-check}
# Check: scaled training features have mean 0 and SD 1
c(max_abs_mean = max(abs(colMeans(sp$X_train))),
  min_sd = min(apply(sp$X_train, 2, sd)),
  max_sd = max(apply(sp$X_train, 2, sd)))
```

```{r save-data, include = FALSE}
save_csvs()   # data/cleaned_full.csv, data/train_scaled.csv, data/test_scaled.csv
```

# Summary statistics

```{r summary-stats}
skewness <- function(x) {     # adjusted Fisher-Pearson skewness
  n <- length(x); z <- (x - mean(x)) / sd(x)
  n / ((n - 1) * (n - 2)) * sum(z^3)
}
q <- function(p) sapply(df[FEATURES], quantile, probs = p, names = FALSE)

summary_stats <- data.frame(
  feature = FEATURES,
  mean    = sapply(df[FEATURES], mean),
  sd      = sapply(df[FEATURES], sd),
  min     = sapply(df[FEATURES], min),
  q1      = q(0.25),
  median  = q(0.50),
  q3      = q(0.75),
  max     = sapply(df[FEATURES], max),
  skew    = sapply(df[FEATURES], skewness),
  row.names = NULL
)
write.csv(summary_stats, file.path(TAB_DIR, "summary_stats.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
kable(summary_stats, digits = 4, caption = "Descriptive statistics, all 569 observations (original units)")
```

Features are on very different scales (e.g. `area_worst` is in the thousands while `fractal_dimension_se` is
around 0.004), which is why standardization is needed before fitting scale-sensitive models. Many features,
especially the `se` features, are right-skewed (skew > 1 for
`r sum(summary_stats$skew > 1)` of 30 features).

## By diagnosis

Cohen's *d* is the difference between the malignant and benign means in pooled-SD units;
`r_with_diagnosis` is the point-biserial correlation with the 0/1 label.

```{r summary-by-dx}
b <- df[df$diagnosis == 0, FEATURES]
m <- df[df$diagnosis == 1, FEATURES]
nb <- nrow(b); nm <- nrow(m)

by_dx <- data.frame(
  feature          = FEATURES,
  benign_mean      = sapply(b, mean),
  benign_sd        = sapply(b, sd),
  benign_median    = sapply(b, median),
  malignant_mean   = sapply(m, mean),
  malignant_sd     = sapply(m, sd),
  malignant_median = sapply(m, median),
  row.names = NULL
)
pooled_sd <- sqrt(((nb - 1) * by_dx$benign_sd^2 + (nm - 1) * by_dx$malignant_sd^2) /
                    (nb + nm - 2))
by_dx$cohens_d         <- (by_dx$malignant_mean - by_dx$benign_mean) / pooled_sd
by_dx$r_with_diagnosis <- sapply(df[FEATURES], cor, y = df$diagnosis)
by_dx <- by_dx[order(-abs(by_dx$cohens_d)), ]
write.csv(by_dx, file.path(TAB_DIR, "summary_by_diagnosis.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

kable(by_dx[, c("feature", "benign_mean", "malignant_mean", "cohens_d", "r_with_diagnosis")],
      digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Features ranked by how strongly they separate malignant from benign")
```

The strongest single separators are `r paste(head(by_dx$feature, 4), collapse = ", ")`
(Cohen's *d* between `r round(min(head(by_dx$cohens_d, 4)), 2)` and `r round(max(head(by_dx$cohens_d, 4)), 2)`).
Features with `d` near zero (`r paste(by_dx$feature[abs(by_dx$cohens_d) < 0.1], collapse = ", ")`)
show almost no difference between classes on their own.

# Distributions

## Histograms

```{r histograms, fig.width = 15, fig.height = 16}
p_hist <- ggplot(long, aes(value, fill = dx)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, position = "identity", alpha = 0.55,
                 color = "#fcfcfb", linewidth = 0.15) +
  facet_wrap(~ feature, ncol = 5, scales = "free") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = DX_COLORS, name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Feature distributions by diagnosis (counts, original units)",
       x = NULL, y = "Count") +
  theme_eda
ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, "histograms.png"), p_hist,
       width = 15, height = 16, dpi = 150, bg = "#fcfcfb")
p_hist
```

## Boxplots by diagnosis

```{r boxplots, fig.width = 15, fig.height = 6.5}
stat_titles <- c(mean = "Mean", se = "Standard error", worst = "Worst")
for (s in STATS) {
  feats <- paste(PROPERTIES, s, sep = "_")
  p_box <- ggplot(long[long$feature %in% feats, ], aes(dx, value, fill = dx)) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.55, alpha = 0.8, color = "#52514e",
                 outlier.shape = 1, outlier.size = 1, outlier.alpha = 0.6) +
    facet_wrap(~ feature, nrow = 2, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = DX_COLORS, guide = "none") +
    labs(title = paste(stat_titles[[s]], "features by diagnosis (original units)"),
         x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_eda
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, paste0("boxplots_", s, ".png")), p_box,
         width = 15, height = 6.5, dpi = 150, bg = "#fcfcfb")
  print(p_box)
}
```

Malignant masses tend to have larger, more irregular nuclei: size (radius, perimeter, area) and contour
features (concavity, concave points, compactness) are clearly shifted upward for malignant cases. Smoothness
and symmetry shift only moderately, with much more overlap between classes, and fractal dimension barely
differs at all.

# Correlations

```{r heatmap, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 10}
cm  <- cor(df[FEATURES])
n_f <- length(FEATURES)
cor_long <- data.frame(
  row_feat = rep(FEATURES, times = n_f),
  col_feat = rep(FEATURES, each = n_f),
  r        = as.vector(cm),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
cor_long$high <- abs(cor_long$r) >= CORR_THRESHOLD & cor_long$row_feat != cor_long$col_feat
cor_long$x <- factor(cor_long$col_feat, levels = FEATURES)
cor_long$y <- factor(cor_long$row_feat, levels = rev(FEATURES))

p_heat <- ggplot(cor_long, aes(x, y, fill = r)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_point(data = cor_long[cor_long$high, ], size = 0.7, color = "#0b0b0b",
             show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(10.5, 20.5), color = "#fcfcfb", linewidth = 1) +   # mean | se | worst
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(10.5, 20.5), color = "#fcfcfb", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#104281", "#3987e5", "#f0efec", "#e34948", "#8f1f1f"),
                       limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Pearson r") +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(title = sprintf("Feature correlation matrix (dots: |r| >= %.1f)", CORR_THRESHOLD),
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 7.5),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.5),
        panel.grid  = element_blank(),
        plot.title  = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#fcfcfb", color = NA))
ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, "correlation_heatmap.png"), p_heat,
       width = 11, height = 10, dpi = 150, bg = "#fcfcfb")
p_heat
```

## Highly correlated feature groups

Two features are linked if |*r*| ≥ `r CORR_THRESHOLD`. A group is every feature connected through such
links (connected components), so a feature belongs to a group even if it is strongly correlated with only
one member.

```{r groups}
hi <- which(upper.tri(cm) & abs(cm) >= CORR_THRESHOLD, arr.ind = TRUE)
pairs <- data.frame(feature_1 = FEATURES[hi[, "row"]],
                    feature_2 = FEATURES[hi[, "col"]],
                    r         = round(cm[hi], 4))
pairs <- pairs[order(-abs(pairs$r)), ]
write.csv(pairs, file.path(TAB_DIR, "high_corr_pairs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Connected components (breadth-first search over the |r| >= threshold graph)
adj <- abs(cm) >= CORR_THRESHOLD
diag(adj) <- FALSE
comp <- rep(NA_integer_, n_f)
k <- 0L
for (i in seq_len(n_f)) {
  if (!is.na(comp[i])) next
  k <- k + 1L
  comp[i] <- k
  queue <- i
  while (length(queue) > 0) {
    v <- queue[1]; queue <- queue[-1]
    nb_idx <- which(adj[v, ] & is.na(comp))
    comp[nb_idx] <- k
    queue <- c(queue, nb_idx)
  }
}
sizes <- tabulate(comp)
multi <- which(sizes > 1)
multi <- multi[order(-sizes[multi], multi)]          # biggest group first
group_name <- setNames(paste0("G", seq_along(multi)), multi)

groups <- data.frame(feature = FEATURES, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
groups$group <- unname(ifelse(sizes[comp] > 1, group_name[as.character(comp)], FEATURES))
groups$group_size <- sizes[comp]
groups$group_members <- sapply(comp, function(cid) paste(FEATURES[comp == cid], collapse = "; "))
groups <- groups[order(groups$group_size == 1, groups$group), ]
write.csv(groups, file.path(TAB_DIR, "correlated_groups.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

group_table <- unique(groups[groups$group_size > 1, c("group", "group_size", "group_members")])
kable(group_table, row.names = FALSE,
      col.names = c("Group", "Size", "Features"),
      caption = sprintf("Feature groups linked by |r| >= %.2f", CORR_THRESHOLD))
```

There are `r nrow(pairs)` feature pairs with |*r*| ≥ `r CORR_THRESHOLD`, which form
`r nrow(group_table)` groups:

- **Size:** radius, perimeter, and area (mean and worst) are nearly redundant. This is expected
  geometrically, since perimeter and area are functions of radius.
- **Contour indentation:** concavity and concave points.
- **Size variability:** the standard errors of radius, perimeter, and area.
- **Texture:** mean and worst texture.

The remaining `r sum(groups$group_size == 1)` features have no partner above the threshold.

**Implications for the modeling sections.** Within a group, features carry largely the same information.
Unregularized models may give unstable or sign-flipped coefficients for group members; lasso tends to keep
one member and drop the others; tree-based importance tends to be split across members. When comparing top
features across methods, picking *different members of the same group* should therefore be read as agreement
on the underlying signal.

```{r top-pairs}
kable(head(pairs, 10), row.names = FALSE, caption = "Ten most correlated pairs")
```
